messages.content:
Several readers answered the same question about machines at work, each pointing at the sentences it used. Decide which answer the evidence supports. Use only the evidence shown; do not use what you know.

Rules:
- An answer is supported only if its evidence states it for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the
  same article and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline, the same condition the question
  states). Evidence about a neighbouring subject does not support an answer.
- When the two rest on texts of different rank, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's
  manual, then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.)
  wins over a ministerial decree (DM). A wording corrected by a corrigendum replaces the original wording.
- For a list, prefer the answer whose items are each stated by the evidence and that leaves none out.
- Readers that found nothing are listed too: when most readers found nothing and the one answer shown rests on evidence about a neighbouring subject, choose "none".
Return JSON only: {"reasoning": "two or three short sentences", "choice": <the number of the answer supported, or "none">}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?

Answer 1 (given by 1 reader(s): facts): "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer under Art. 18 of the Regulation, and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery solely for its own use is not considered a manufacturer."
Under Article 18 of the Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification (one that affects the safety of only the machinery or a related product in an assembly) becomes subject to the manufacturer's obligations and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility; a non-professional user modifying machinery for its own use is excluded.
Evidence:
- non-professional user modifying machinery for own use: becomesManufacturer = shall not be considered to be a manufacturer (condition: for his or her own use) | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]
- natural or legal person carrying out substantial modification: hasObligation = shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 (condition: if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery) | sentence: "Article 18 Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product or, if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery, for that affected machinery or related product, as demonstrated in the risk assessment." [REG, Art. 18]
- person who carries out substantial modification: hasObligation = ensure and declare on its sole responsibility | sentence: "The person who carries out the substantial modification shall in particular, but without prejudice to other obligations set out in Article 10, ensure and declare on its sole responsibility that the machinery or related product concerned is in conformity with the applicable requirements of this Regulation and shall apply the relevant conformity assessment procedure as provided in Article 25 (2), (3) and (4) of this Regulation." [REG, Art. 18]

Answer 2 (given by 1 reader(s): words): "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (a non-professional user modifying for their own use is excluded)."
Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (REG), any natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery is considered its manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations. A non-professional user who modifies their own machinery for their own use is not treated as a manufacturer.
Evidence:
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10" [REG, Art. 18]
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation" [REG, Art. 18]

Answer 3 (given by 1 reader(s): similar): "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery or related product is considered the manufacturer (REG Art. 18), except a non-professional user modifying for their own use."
Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (REG), any natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product is considered its manufacturer, unless it is a non-professional user modifying the machinery for their own use.
Evidence:
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation" [REG, Art. 18]
- Read on demand: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation" [REG, Art. 18]

Answer 4 (given by 1 reader(s): search): "The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (not the original manufacturer, unless it is a non-professional user modifying for own use)."
Under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation), the person who carries out a substantial modification of machinery is considered to be the manufacturer and must meet the manufacturer's obligations under Article 10 for that machinery; a non-professional user modifying for their own use is excluded.
Evidence:
- Found by search: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "Article 18 Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product" [REG, Art. 18]

Readers that found nothing: none

response.text: {"reasoning": "All four answers rest on REG Art. 18, which says the person carrying out a substantial modification is considered the manufacturer, with a non-professional user modifying for own use excluded. Answer 1 is the most complete, with each part stated in the evidence: Art. 10 obligations, the sole-responsibility declaration, and the non-professional exclusion. Answers 2-4 say the same in less detail, so the answers agree and Answer 1 is fully supported.", "choice": 1}
